contents.text:
I'm reading the LouisAgent CLI doc for how CliHost builds the engine and hands it to ConsoleChat, and ADR 0091 for HostServices. I'm checking how one-shot and interactive runs are chosen from the prompt arguments.

I'm skipping the ShowPage lookup, since the page doesn't give me exact section addresses to point at. I'll cite the CliHost and HostServices docs directly instead.

This program starts the coding agent in the terminal. It names what the agent loads, then hands that to a host that runs it.

The `using` lines bring in the namespaces. Most come from the framework: `LouisAgent.Core.Web`, `.Anthropic`, `.Ollama`, `.OpenAi`, `.Telemetry`, `.Hosting`, and `LouisAgent.Cli`. The last one, `LouisAgent.Coding`, is the demo's own catalogue.

The call that does the work is `CliHost.RunAsync`. It takes three things: the command-line `args`, the catalogue, and the host services. `CliHost` is the one call a program makes. It builds the engine with `AgentHost.Build`, then runs it, either once for a prompt or as an interactive chat. (`src/docs/projects/LouisAgent.Cli.md`)

`CodingCatalog.Create()` is the catalogue. It names the identities and packs this program can load. The coding agent's catalogue names three identities and nine packs. It is the program's own file, not the framework's. (`src/docs/guides/build-an-identity.md`)

`new HostServices(...)` lends the agent what the host provides. Here that is three things:

- `WebAccess.Create`, the web.
- `OtlpTelemetry.Instance`, the telemetry.
- The `Providers` array: Anthropic, Ollama and the OpenAI-compatible provider, the models it can talk to.

A program composes these through `HostServices`, and core names none of the libraries behind them. (`src/docs/adr/0091-web-access-and-telemetry-are-libraries-on-core.md`)

The comment at the top gives the usage: `LouisAgent.CodingCli [prompt]`. Pass a prompt and it answers once. Pass none and it opens the chat.

Sources: `src/docs/projects/LouisAgent.Cli.md`, `src/docs/adr/0091-web-access-and-telemetry-are-libraries-on-core.md`, `src/docs/guides/build-an-identity.md`.
